specGaps: GAP (maxReaders has no source at serve time) — §2.1's parallel.maxReaders lives in the TARGET repo's .conductor/config.json, but serve.py runs before any target repo is chosen and cannot read one. RESOLUTION: scripts/conductor_wiring.py owns the §2.1 default (6, plan:583) as ONE named module constant that the derivation consumes; serve.py may override it with an explicit flag that persists in serve-session.json exactly like host/port; Task 12.2's setup probe remains the per-repo enforcement (observed slots >= that repo's configured maxReaders). CROSS-TASK OBLIGATION recorded for the Phase 12 gate: 12.2 writes .conductor/config.json and must use the SAME literal, or the two defaults drift apart in a way no test in either task would see.

GAP (the derivation formula is never given) — the plan mandates that --parallel and maxInflightPerModel come from 'the SAME number' but states no formula, and §2.2's example shows maxInflightPerModel 4 next to §2.1's maxReaders 6. RESOLUTION: slots == maxInflightPerModel == max(1, maxReaders). Equality trivially satisfies §2.2's 'MUST be <= llama-server's slot count' with zero drift, and the 4-vs-6 in the plan's two examples is read as illustrative hand-editability, not a mandated ratio. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: slots = maxReaders + maxImplementers + 1 (readers, writers and the orchestrator all issue upstream traffic). It is arguably more accurate about real demand, but it introduces a second number where the plan's whole point was one, and it would let admission admit fewer than the slots available — safe, but no longer 'derived from the same number'. Recorded so the Phase 12 gate can revisit it with the measured slot count in hand rather than re-deriving it blind.

GAP (per-slot context) — NEW, found while verifying the flag rather than assuming it: llama-server's help says --kv-unified is 'enabled if number of slots is auto', so passing an explicit --parallel N leaves the auto branch and can divide the served context among N slots. Nothing in the plan mentions this, and silently serving a sixth of the configured context would present as random truncation deep inside agent prompts. RESOLUTION: the argv derivation is context-aware and its exact form is decided by evidence collected INSIDE this same task — row 12.1-live-ctx-per-slot records the server's reported per-slot context for three startups (no --parallel; --parallel N; --parallel N plus whatever flag preserves the unified buffer), and row 12.1-ctx-per-slot-preserved pins the argv that the recorded evidence shows preserves the configured per-slot context, with slots == 1 required to be an identity case either way. If the probe shows no split, the pinned argv is just --parallel N and the row still holds; nothing is guessed in advance.

GAP (the router config is generated AND hand-editable) — §2.2:636 calls .data/configs/conductor-router.json 'generated by serve.py, hand-editable', and 11.8 hand-writes that exact path before 12.1 exists. Regenerating it wholesale every run destroys those edits. RESOLUTION: serve.py OWNS exactly the machine-derived keys — version, listen.host, listen.port, upstream.host, upstream.port, admission.maxInflightPerModel, metrics.ledgerPath — and preserves every other key found in an existing file (maxQueued, queueTimeoutMs, priorities, affinity, schema, logging). It is the same merge primitive as the fragment merge with the precedence reversed, not a second implementation. `--fresh` regenerates from scratch, matching how --fresh already ignores serve-session.json.

GAP (nothing in the plugin can find the router) — the committed router client takes RouterClientConfig {listen:{host,port}, probeTimeoutMs}, core Config has no router block, opencode rejects unrecognized config keys (serve.py:223), and no TS file at HEAD reads any LLAMA_HARNESS_* variable or the router config path. Without a channel, the plugin cannot probe health, cannot fetch metrics, and cannot tell a --no-router session from a router session — which would make G5's failover machinery unreachable. RESOLUTION: serve.py exports the channel as session ENV, alongside the LLAMA_HARNESS_MODEL / _URL / _SERVER_PID variables it already writes into the rcfile: LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER (1/0), LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER_URL, LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER_CONFIG (absolute path to the generated file). Env is chosen precisely because it needs no opencode config key and no §2.1 schema widening; the consuming TS lands with whichever task first needs it (10.1 or 13.1), and 12.1 only guarantees the variables exist and are correct.

GAP (the generated ledger path is relative) — §2.2's literal '.data/router/metrics.jsonl' resolves against the ROUTER process's cwd, which under a detached supervisor is inherited from whatever the user's shell was in. RESOLUTION: the generated ledgerPath is absolute (<repo>/.data/router/metrics.jsonl) AND the supervisor launches the router with cwd == the repo root, so a hand-edited relative path resolves to the same place. Belt and braces because a metrics ledger written into a random cwd is invisible rather than broken, and the POC's dataset is the deliverable.

GAP (--schema has no search path, and the file is gitignored) — C-041 makes --schema required with no fallback, but src/tests/schemas/RouterConfig.schema.json is generated by scripts/test-conductor.sh and ignored by .gitignore:28, so a fresh clone has no schema file and the router cannot start. RESOLUTION: a pure preflight decision function returns one of {launch, fall-back-direct, refuse}. Auto default (no flag) + missing schema -> fall back to a direct session with a loud notice, because G5 says a missing router must never cost the user their session. Explicit --router + missing schema -> refuse with a named remedy (`node conductor/tools/export-schemas.ts src/tests/schemas`), because the user asked for the thing that cannot be provided. serve.py may run the exporter itself when node is available; the DECISION is what is unit-tested.

GAP (--no-shell cannot host a supervisor) — serve.py --no-shell execs into llama-server (serve.py:485-488), so there is no surviving python and no shell pid for a supervisor to poll; a router launched there would outlive everything or die immediately. RESOLUTION: --no-shell never launches the router, and --no-shell together with an explicit --router exits with a message naming the incompatibility rather than launching an unsupervisable process. This is also the mode Step 2's live measurement runs in, which is consistent: those probes measure llama-server, not the router.

GAP (fragment-aware base config is undefined) — the plan says fetch_models' `config` subcommand 'regenerates the fragment-aware base config' without defining the term. RESOLUTION: generate_opencode_config's output passes through the SAME merge + substitution used at session time, so the base config already carries the conductor wiring and `fetch_models config` can never strip it out from under a live session; the session-time merge over an already-merged base is a no-op by the idempotence row. The base config keeps the DIRECT llama-server baseURL — the router rewrite is a session-time decision, since the base config is written when no router port has been resolved.

GAP (array merge semantics) — 'deep merge, conductor keys win' does not say what happens to arrays. RESOLUTION: dicts merge recursively; every non-dict value, arrays included, is REPLACED by the conductor value. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: unioning the `plugin` array so a user's own plugins survive. It is friendlier, but it is a special case in a function whose predictability is the point, and the base config is machine-generated by fetch_models and carries no plugin key at HEAD (verified: keys are exactly $schema/provider/model/small_model). Recorded here so a future user-supplied base with its own plugins is a known, not a surprise.

assertions.text: generate_router_config in scripts/conductor_wiring.py is a pure function of the resolved router host/port, upstream host/port and derived slot count, and returns the §2.2 document (plan:639-669) exactly: version 1; listen/upstream carrying the host and port it was given; admission {maxInflightPerModel: the derived slots, maxQueued 64, queueTimeoutMs 600000}; priorities {interactive 0, review 1, batch 2}; affinity {header 'X-Conductor-Group', contiguousDequeue true}; schema {observeHeader 'X-Conductor-Schema', validateResponses true, rejectOnMissing FALSE}; metrics.ledgerPath; logging.level 'info'. The test additionally asserts NO 'batching' key at any depth (G13, plan:648-650) and that queueTimeoutMs is strictly less than §2.1's parallel.subSessionTimeoutMs default of 900000, so a queue timeout can only ever report as itself. The function performs no I/O — it returns a dict and writes nothing

the generated dict is checked against the EXPORTED schema file src/tests/schemas/RouterConfig.schema.json — the single source, not a shape retyped in Python: for the document and for every nested object, set(generated.keys()) equals set(schema.properties.keys()) (the schema sets additionalProperties:false at every level, so equality is the correct relation, not containment), every name in the schema's `required` list is present, and each leaf's JSON type matches the schema's declared type. A MISSING schema file FAILS the test with a message naming the file and the regeneration command; it never skips (G4, and scripts/test-conductor.sh rejects skip directives outright). Both ports are additionally asserted inside src/router/config.hpp's accepted range 1..65535

ONE pure function of ONE number is the only source of both concurrency numbers: called with a maxReaders value it yields a slot count that is used verbatim as llama-server's `--parallel <slots>` AND as the generated router config's admission.maxInflightPerModel. The test drives several maxReaders values through the single call path and asserts, at each: build_server_command's argv contains '--parallel' exactly once immediately followed by that slot count as a string; the router config generated in the same call carries maxInflightPerModel equal to the same integer; maxInflightPerModel <= slots holds; and changing the one input changes both outputs in lockstep. It also asserts that at HEAD's serve.py the argv had NO --parallel, so the row is proving a new argument rather than restating an existing one

the derivation is total and can never emit a zero: maxReaders values of 0 and of a negative integer both yield slots of 1 (never '--parallel 0', which would ask llama-server for zero slots, and never admission.maxInflightPerModel 0, which would make the router admit nothing and deadlock every session behind it) — a reachable case, since C-031 records a maxReaders of 0 silently dispatching zero reviewers in committed code. A non-integer or None input raises a named error rather than propagating into an argv string

the served per-slot context is preserved when slots > 1: the argv derivation emits, alongside '--parallel <slots>', whatever the live observation recorded in 12.1-live-ctx-per-slot shows is required to keep llama-server's per-slot context at the configured value (llama-server --help: --kv-unified is 'enabled if number of slots is auto', so an explicit --parallel leaves that branch). The unittest pins the exact resulting argv against the recorded observation, cited by its line in src/router/UPSTREAM_CONTRACT.md, and asserts the identity case: at slots == 1 the argv is byte-identical to HEAD's build_server_command output plus '--parallel 1' and nothing else. This row may not be closed on reasoning about the flag — only on the recorded measurement

metrics.ledgerPath in the generated config is the ABSOLUTE path <repo root>/.data/router/metrics.jsonl (not §2.2's bare relative literal), and the supervisor launches llama-router with cwd set to the repo root, so a hand-edited relative path resolves to the same file. The test asserts os.path.isabs on the generated value, that it ends with '.data/router/metrics.jsonl', that the repo root component is the realpath'd root (no symlink component), and that the recorded launch cwd equals that root — because Task 11.7's ledger writer creates the parent directory wherever the path points, so a wrong cwd produces a silently misplaced ledger rather than an error

regeneration over an EXISTING .data/configs/conductor-router.json overwrites only the machine-derived keys and preserves every hand edit: given a file whose admission.maxQueued, admission.queueTimeoutMs, priorities, affinity, schema and logging blocks have been altered by hand, the regenerated document carries those altered values unchanged while version, listen.host, listen.port, upstream.host, upstream.port, admission.maxInflightPerModel and metrics.ledgerPath are refreshed from the current run. With no existing file, the full §2.2 document is written. With --fresh, the file is regenerated from scratch and the hand edits are dropped — the same semantics --fresh already has for serve-session.json. This is the fragment merge primitive with the precedence reversed, not a second merge implementation, and Task 11.8 hand-writes this exact path before 12.1 first runs

merge_opencode_fragment deep-merges conductor/opencode-fragment.json into a base opencode config dict: nested dicts merge recursively so base-only keys survive at every depth (a base provider block with its models map and options comes through untouched), on any conflicting key the CONDUCTOR value wins, and every non-dict value — arrays included — is REPLACED rather than concatenated. The merged result carries the fragment's plugin array and all seven conductor-* agent definitions with tools.task false on each, and the base's $schema / provider / model / small_model keys are all still present with their original values

the merge is idempotent and non-mutating: merging the fragment into an ALREADY-merged config yields a result equal to the first merge (asserted on the serialized JSON, so key order is included), which is what makes it safe for the session-time merge to run over the fragment-aware base config; and neither the base dict nor the fragment dict passed in is modified — the caller's objects compare equal to deep copies taken before the call, so the fragment loaded once can be reused for a second merge without carrying state across

every ${LLAMA_HARNESS_ROOT} occurrence is substituted with this repo's absolute realpath'd root at generation time, at any depth and in any string (the plugin path and the '{file:...}' prompt reference both): the serialized merged config contains ZERO remaining '${LLAMA_HARNESS_ROOT}' substrings, the plugin entry equals <root>/conductor/plugin/index.ts, the orchestrator agent's prompt equals '{file:<root>/conductor/doctrine/core.md}', and the root used has no symlink component (os.path.realpath of it equals itself — the macOS /var vs /private/var trap recorded in wire-notes). A leftover token is fatal rather than cosmetic: opencode scans every config string for brace-file references and a dangling one is a hard ConfigInvalidError

generation VERIFIES that every substituted '{file:<path>}' target and the substituted plugin path exist on disk, and raises a named error identifying the missing path when one does not — a config referencing a missing file makes opencode's config endpoint return 400 so that NO session can start (wire-notes.md:31), which would present to the user as opencode being broken rather than as a conductor wiring fault. The test drives both directions: with the real repo the check passes for conductor/plugin/index.ts and conductor/doctrine/core.md; with a fragment pointing at a non-existent doctrine file the error names that exact path

the generated session config pins opencode auto-update OFF — 'autoupdate': false at the top level — so the wire contract verified against 1.18.15 cannot drift under a running session (C-012 ruling, CORRECTIONS.md:150). The key name is the one documented by the shipped 1.18.15 binary's own config reference ('"autoupdate": true | false | "notify"'), which matters because serve.py:223 records that opencode rejects configs carrying unrecognized keys. The test asserts the key is present and false in the merged session config, and that an explicit 'autoupdate' already present in the base is overridden to false

with the router enabled, the merged session config's provider.llamacpp.options.baseURL is rewritten to the ROUTER origin — 'http://<listen.host>:<listen.port>/v1' — and the port in that string is the SAME resolved integer that the router config generated in the same call carries at listen.port, so there is one number in both places. The rewrite reuses the committed write_session_opencode_config path (serve.py:213-217) rather than editing the provider block a second time, and the rest of the provider options (apiKey, timeout, headerTimeout) are unchanged

--no-router leaves the merged session config's baseURL pointing DIRECTLY at llama-server ('http://<server host>:<server port>/v1') and changes nothing else: the test merges both ways from the same base and asserts the two resulting configs are equal at every key EXCEPT provider.llamacpp.options.baseURL — the plugin array, all seven agents, autoupdate, model and small_model are identical. That structural equality is what makes '--no-router runs the identical workflow' (§0.3, G5) a property rather than a claim

serve.py's write_session_opencode_config remains the ONLY writer of .data/configs/opencode.session.json: the fragment merge, the substitution and the baseURL decision all happen inside that one function, its existing behaviour is retained (it still loads .data/configs/opencode.json, still SystemExits with the 'run: scripts/fetch_models.py config' remedy when that base is absent or unparseable, and still sets model/small_model to the served id when the id appears in provider.models), and no second session-config path or file appears anywhere in the diff

`fetch_models.py config` (cmd_config -> regenerate_configs -> generate_opencode_config) writes a fragment-aware BASE .data/configs/opencode.json: the written document carries the substituted plugin path, all seven agents and autoupdate false, produced by the SAME merge function the session path uses (one implementation, asserted by the test calling the same symbol), while its baseURL stays DIRECT at the llama-server host/port it was given, because no router port has been resolved at that point. Consequently running `fetch_models config` mid-session can no longer strip conductor wiring out of the base config, and a session-time merge over that base is a no-op (12.1-merge-idempotent-nonmutating)

the --router/--no-router default resolves through a pure decision function over the full matrix (flag absent | --router | --no-router) x (binary found | not found): absent + found -> router; absent + not found -> direct, with a notice; --router + not found -> refuse with a message naming the searched locations; --no-router -> direct regardless. The binary search itself is a pure function of an injected root and env mapping with a PINNED order — $LLAMA_ROUTER (used only when it names an existing executable file), then <root>/.out/build/clang-relwdebinfo/llama-router, then clang-release, then clang-debug, then <root>/.data/tools/llama-router, then PATH — and the test drives it against a temp root with binaries planted in different slots. fetch_models.find_tool is NOT reused here: its env branch is hard-coded to llama-server and its own-tools branch looks only in .data/tools, while CMakePresets.json:9 puts the router in .out/build/<preset>/

the router preflight decision is a pure function returning one of launch / fall-back-direct / refuse, and it honours C-041's contract that --schema is REQUIRED with no search path: with the exported src/tests/schemas/RouterConfig.schema.json ABSENT (the normal state of a fresh clone — .gitignore:28 ignores that directory and scripts/test-conductor.sh generates it), the auto default falls back to a DIRECT session with a loud notice rather than costing the user their session, while an EXPLICIT --router refuses with a message naming the remedy `node conductor/tools/export-schemas.ts src/tests/schemas`. With the schema present and the binary found, the decision is launch and the resolved schema path is the absolute path to that file

the restart delay is a PURE function of (consecutive crashes, last run's uptime) with the four constants named in conductor_wiring.py: base 500 ms, factor 2, cap 30000 ms, healthy threshold 60 s. The test drives a crash / crash / crash / healthy-run / crash sequence and asserts 500, 1000, 2000, then back to 500 after the healthy run; it asserts the delay never exceeds 30000 however many consecutive crashes are fed in (including a large count, so an overflow or an unbounded shift would be caught); and it uses no real clock, spawns no process and sleeps not at all

the supervisor's restart DECISION is a pure function of the router's exit status and honours C-041's pinned exit codes rather than restarting blindly: exit 0 (clean shutdown after SIGINT/SIGTERM) -> do not restart; exit 2 (usage) , 3 (ConfigError) and 4 (listen bind failure) -> FATAL, do not restart, and surface a message that carries the router's stderr verbatim (which C-041 guarantees names the offending flag, the ConfigError::field(), or host:port respectively); any other exit status or a termination by signal -> restart after the backoff delay. Restarting on 3 in particular would spin forever on a config that will never parse while hiding the one message that names the broken field

with the router enabled and a session shell in play, serve.py launches llama-router under a small DETACHED supervisor process — serve.py itself execs into the shell (serve.py:511-516) and cannot supervise anything (§4.4) — and the supervisor: invokes the C-041 argv `<router binary> --config <generated absolute path> --schema <exported absolute path>` with cwd at the repo root; is started with start_new_session=True and DEVNULL stdio, mirroring start_watchdog (serve.py:359-376) rather than inventing a second lifecycle; polls the SHELL pid and, when it disappears, sends the router SIGTERM, waits a bounded grace, then SIGKILL, so no router outlives the session; and restarts a crashed router per the backoff and exit-code policies. `--no-shell` launches NO router and NO supervisor (there is no surviving python and no shell pid after serve.py:487's execv), and `--no-shell --router` together exit with a message naming the incompatibility. The argv, cwd, flags and signal sequence are asserted through an injected spawn seam so the unittest starts no process

no session is ever handed a config pointing at a router that is not up: the session opencode config is written only AFTER the routing decision is final, and if the launched router does not answer GET /conductor/health within the bounded readiness wait, serve.py falls back to the DIRECT baseURL, prints a loud notice, and does not leave a supervisor chasing a router the session is not using. The test drives the decision function with a health probe seam returning healthy / never-healthy / connection-refused and asserts the resulting baseURL and router-enabled flag in each case. This is the startup half of G5 that the plugin's mid-session failover (Task 7.2) structurally cannot cover — a session whose every request 502s from the first prompt never gets far enough to fail over

the session env block is a pure function whose output is used by BOTH the rcfile serve.py writes and its --print-env output, and with the router enabled it carries LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER=1, LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER_URL=http://<listen.host>:<listen.port> and LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER_CONFIG=<absolute path to the generated config>, alongside the existing LLAMA_HARNESS_MODEL / _URL / _SERVER_PID; with --no-router (or after the readiness fallback) LLAMA_HARNESS_ROUTER is 0 and the URL variable is absent. Env is the channel because opencode rejects unrecognized config keys (serve.py:223) and core Config has no router block, so nothing in the committed TS can otherwise learn the router's listen host/port (verified: no conductor/ source reads LLAMA_HARNESS_* or conductor-router.json at HEAD). The test asserts the dict for both modes and that the generated rcfile text exports every variable in it

scripts/test-conductor.sh gains a python leg — `/usr/bin/python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` — placed AFTER the §11.1 schema-export leg (so src/tests/schemas is fresh for the parity row) and BEFORE the final 'GATE PASS', failing the gate on any failure or error and printing the failing output. The tests import scripts/conductor_wiring.py directly, run under python 3.9.6 (no 3.10+ syntax), and touch only tempfile directories: the whole leg starts no server, opens no socket, spawns no llama-server or llama-router, and writes nothing under .data/ or .out/ — asserted by the tests' own use of an injected root and spawn seam rather than the real paths

LIVE — MANDATORY DEFERRED BINDING (HANDOFF 'Deferred bindings'; UPSTREAM_CONTRACT.md Step 2 item 6, the load-bearing number C-041 says 11.8 could not produce): against a live llama-server started through scripts/serve.py --no-shell on qwen3.6-27b, issue N concurrent trivial completions for N in {1,2,4,8} in TWO configurations — the default (NO --parallel, which llama-server's help says means slots = auto, so the baseline slot count is READ from the server's startup output and recorded, never assumed to be 1) and with the derived `--parallel <slots>`. The section records verbatim command lines, cwd, and raw output including per-request wall-clock times, and states for each configuration the N at which latency starts scaling linearly — the effective concurrent slot count. The recorded number is then stated as the constraint on parallel.maxReaders / admission.maxInflightPerModel / serve.py's --parallel derivation, and if it is BELOW the wiring's default of 6 the default is lowered to the measured value in this same task and the change recorded as a deviation

LIVE — the per-slot context observation that decides 12.1-ctx-per-slot-preserved: llama-server is started THREE times with the same model and the same configured context, and the startup output that reports the context per slot/sequence is pasted verbatim for each — (a) no --parallel (auto slots, unified KV enabled per the binary's own help), (b) `--parallel <slots>`, (c) `--parallel <slots>` plus the flag that restores the unified KV buffer. The section states, in plain words, whether an explicit --parallel divides the served context and which argv keeps the per-slot context at the configured value. Nothing about this is inferred from the help text alone — the help line ('--kv-unified ... default: enabled if number of slots is auto') is what made the probe necessary, not what settles it

LIVE — UPSTREAM_CONTRACT.md Step 2 item 5, the other item C-041 leaves to this task: a request naming a model that is NOT currently resident is issued in router mode (--models-preset with --models-max 1) and the section records the verbatim request, the raw response, and the measured load latency (wall-clock from request to first byte, plus the server-side load lines from the log), so the autoload cost is a measured number rather than a shrug. If the second model cannot be made non-resident, or the probe cannot run for any other reason, the section records BLOCKED plus the exact commands attempted

LIVE — the binding is discharged honestly or not at all: src/router/UPSTREAM_CONTRACT.md's `WIRE_CONTRACT_VERIFIED: <pending — see status>` line is replaced with a real dated stamp ONLY when all six Step 2 items are covered somewhere in the file — items 1-4 by Task 11.8's appended section (which row 11.8-binding-not-discharged deliberately left the stamp pending for) and items 5-6 by this task's rows — and the stamp names which task observed which item; if ANY item is BLOCKED the stamp stays pending and says so. M8 discipline over the whole addition, checkable by a reader who was not present: every command is a full copy-pasteable line with its cwd, every output block is raw stdout/stderr including exit codes and is never re-wrapped or summarized, every version and path is the observed one (llama-server build line, model id, config paths), and no number appears that was not printed by something. The orchestrator re-runs at least one recorded command and diffs the result before the stamp is accepted
